implementerProof.whatTheProofDidNotCover: No row of any round drives a lone runner over several of its own ticks. The two-runner rows stop both runners inside the first pass, and the staggered-start row observes exactly two ticks. The period gate's tie-break against its own ticker (failure 1) is invisible to all of them, and shows up in about a third of the ticks of a single process.

failures.criterion: Acceptance 1: "each background loop behaving as the plan's table says". A leased loop must make its pass every period. At one process - which is what this deployment runs today, and what every deployment runs between rolls - it now makes about two passes in three.
failures.evidence: Measured on the real surface with nothing else on the database: `go test -count=3 -run TestProbeOneRunnerMakesAPassOnEveryTick ./internal/dispatch/api/` driving RunSuggestionOutcomeSweep for ten ticks of one second, three times over — `ran 7, skipped 3`, `ran 6, skipped 4`, `ran 6, skipped 4`. Each skip is an interval of that loop's work no pass of any process made: the lease was free and no other process existed. I met it in the browser suite's own envoy-dispatch log, which is a single process: its ticks at 09:03:13.315 ran, 09:04:13.318 ran, 09:05:13.300 skipped, 09:06:13.319 ran, 09:07:13.324 ran — the skipped tick fired 18 ms earlier than the one before it. The mechanism is arithmetic, not a race: every leased loop ticks on the very interval it passes as its period (RunSuggestionOutcomeSweep, redeliver.Sweeper.Run, duty.RunJittered's callers), and `began_at` is stamped when the pass starts, a few milliseconds after the tick that made it — the time it takes to take the lease (duty/exclusive.go, periodServed then pass then recordPassOn). The gate asks `began_at > now() - make_interval(secs => period)`. Two consecutive ticks are one period apart, so whether the previous pass's record falls inside this tick's window is decided entirely by whether this tick's acquire delay is shorter than the previous tick's. Migration 0115's own comment anticipated the neighbouring error — a period measured from the pass's end would be short by the pass's duration — and recording `began_at` at the start is what fixes that one and makes the two spans exactly equal, which is what turns the comparison into a tie-break on jitter. The loops affected are all six: the suggestion-outcome sweep (1 min), the webhook redelivery sweep (2 min), the reference-excerpt reconciliation (its 2 s converging step included), the architecture import and the delivery reconcile (5 min), and the daily document compaction, which loses a whole day when its tick is the one dropped. Pinned by the red test TestALoneRunnerMakesAPassOnEveryTick in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/suggestion_outcomes_lease_test.go (commit a21eb163), beside the existing two-runner row: it drives ten real ticks of one runner and asserts no skip, and is red here at `ran 6, skipped 4`. Not prescribing the fix; two shapes exist — judge the period from the tick that fired rather than from the read that follows it, since the loop already knows when it ticked, or allow the gate the gap between a tick and its record — and the first needs no tolerance constant.

proof.criterion: Round 3's first claim: a leased pass that a shutdown cuts short serves no period, and the process still up makes that pass — which is what a rolling update's SIGTERM mid-pass needs, since the alternative is a maintenance window nobody covers.
proof.surface: Two real envoy-dispatch binaries on one Postgres 17 and one nats-server 2.10 in this issue's pod, with a loopback GitHub that holds the webhook sweep's first delivery listing so a process can be SIGTERMed while it is inside its pass, and counts those listings so the surviving process's work is measured from outside the servers rather than from its own log.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && . /legion/harness/env.sh && go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 30m -run 'TestProbeAPassSIGTERMedMidWorkLeavesItsPeriodForTheSurvivor|TestProbeAFinishedPassStillServesItsPeriodForTheSurvivor' ./cmd/dispatch   (throwaway probes, removed before this handoff)
proof.observed: A took the lease and blocked inside the GitHub listing while B logged the skip. SIGTERM to A: it exited 39 ms later, logged `dispatch duty: leased pass cut short by shutdown; its period is left unserved` for lease=webhook-redelivery, and logged no pass that ran. B made the sweep 1 m 59.9 s after the SIGTERM — one redeliver.Interval — and the delivery listings went 1 → 2, so B did the work rather than only reporting it.
proof.negativeControl: The other half of the same claim in the same rig, which is the deliberate difference: when the first pass is allowed to finish instead of being cut short, the second process reports skipped=1 and the listings stay at 1. The only thing that differs between the two rows is whether the first pass was interrupted.
